headline: High: CrewAI’s default write/network privileges can drive OpenBBTerminal into unsafe downstream actions; shared workspace also creates prompt-injection and data-leakage risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and uses shared memory by default, so attacker-controlled files or outputs can be fed into OpenBBTerminal if the pair shares a workspace. OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST/FastAPI surfaces and “connect once, consume everywhere,” making instruction-like content more likely to be reused. No explicit provenance tracking is shown for either agent.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working directory or shared file drop, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF OpenBBTerminal consumes CrewAI-generated files or messages as instructions without provenance checks, hijack risk increases.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories.
Disable automatic ingestion of CrewAI outputs by OpenBBTerminal.
Add a manual review step before any file or message is treated as instructions.
Use a provenance tag or allowlist for inputs.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI touches developer-passed crew data and can write/read the host filesystem; OpenBBTerminal handles financial, licensed, and public data and can expose it through APIs/MCP. If they share a workspace, sensitive inputs from CrewAI can be surfaced to OpenBBTerminal outputs or API calls. The profiles do not show isolation by default, so leakage is plausible in default pair deployments.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem or notebook workspace, file-based leakage is possible.
IF OpenBBTerminal sends queried data to external APIs or MCP consumers, CrewAI-passed secrets may be exposed.
mitigations: Keep sensitive CrewAI inputs out of shared folders.
Run OpenBBTerminal with a separate workspace and credentials.
Review API/MCP destinations before enabling them.
Redact secrets before passing data between agents.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and secret-scanning on handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI has broad filesystem write and subprocess execution, while OpenBBTerminal can run MCP/REST/FastAPI services and consume data in a “connect once, consume everywhere” pattern. Even though OpenBBTerminal lacks filesystem write, both can mutate shared runtime state through files, services, or local ports if co-located. The overlap is enough for default coordination bugs, though not the highest-risk write/write collision.
conditions: IF both agents target the same local port, config file, or shared cache, state conflicts can occur.
IF CrewAI subprocesses modify files that OpenBBTerminal reads concurrently, race conditions are reachable.
mitigations: Assign separate ports and config paths.
Avoid shared mutable files between the agents.
Serialize access to any common cache or dataset.
Run one agent at a time for shared resources.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state and port allocation.

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI can generate outputs from tool-using agents, and OpenBBTerminal is positioned to consume data through APIs/MCP with a “connect once, consume everywhere” workflow. If OpenBBTerminal treats CrewAI outputs as authoritative, erroneous or manipulated facts can cascade into financial analysis or downstream actions. Because the pair lacks documented verification boundaries, uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal ingests CrewAI-produced summaries without independent verification, cascading error is reachable.
IF CrewAI outputs are used to drive financial decisions or reports, the blast radius includes multiple work products.
mitigations: Require source citations before OpenBBTerminal accepts CrewAI output.
Add a human review gate for any financial recommendation.
Compare CrewAI outputs against raw data before acting.
Limit CrewAI to drafting, not deciding.
requires-engineering: implement validation rules and confidence thresholds on handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data. If EU or regulated financial data is routed through CrewAI’s broader tool stack or shared logs, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so the mismatch is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is passed from OpenBBTerminal into CrewAI logs or prompts, retention risk appears.
IF either agent stores data longer than the other, subject-rights or retention mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through CrewAI prompts.
Align retention settings across both tools.
Document where logs are stored and who can access them.
Purge temporary files after each run.
requires-engineering: add policy controls for residency, retention, and deletion.
